title: One Hosepipe Between Us
subject: a man on an allotment who shares one hosepipe through the fence with the woman on the next plot, and starts leaving tomatoes on her shed step every Sunday until she leaves a note asking him to dinner
caption: Rockabilly revival, 1950s Sun Records style. Hollow-body electric guitar with tape slapback and twangy lead fills, slapped upright bass clicking on every beat, brushed snare with rimshots, rolling barrelhouse piano. Warm live-room mono production with tape echo. Male baritone, clearly sung melody with playful hiccups. 172 BPM, E major. Sweet, grinning, smitten. No synths, no autotune, no trap hi-hats, no distorted metal guitar, no modern pop drums.
lyrics:
[Intro - slapback guitar, slapped bass]

[Verse 1]
There's a gap in the fence on plot nineteen
And a green hosepipe running in between
You water your beans, then you pass it through
And I water mine with the hose still warm from you

[Pre-Chorus]
You wave your trowel, I tip my hat
Nobody's ever been sweeter than that

[Chorus]
One hosepipe between us, honey
One tap and a rusty key
I leave tomatoes on your shed step
Every Sunday, two or three

[Verse 2]
You fixed the leak with a rubber band
I said you've got a clever hand
You laughed so loud the robins ran
And I dropped my watering can

[Pre-Chorus]
The runner beans are climbing high
I'm climbing too and I don't know why

[Chorus]
One hosepipe between us, honey
One tap and a rusty key
Today a note was on my shed step
Friday dinner, you and me

[Outro - piano roll, guitar tag]
One hosepipe, two sheds, and a Friday tea
